column3: The Hebrew calls these the sons of Aaron; BSB first uses descendants and then sons.
The Hebrew joins David, Zadok, and Ahimelech in dividing the groups; BSB explicitly presents Zadok and Ahimelech as helping David.
The Hebrew uses active plural dividing agents; BSB describes their being divided passively. It repeatedly calls the families fathers’ houses.
The Hebrew uses active plural dividing agents and says these with those; BSB uses a passive division by lot.
The Hebrew says Shemaiah wrote them, without an explicit names noun, and repeats taken for Ithamar; BSB supplies names and omits that repetition.
The Hebrew describes Aaron’s mediation with his hand and calls him their father; BSB uses regulations prescribed by their forefather.
The Hebrew calls these the remaining sons of Levi; BSB uses descendants.
The Hebrew repeats Rehabiah’s name and calls Isshiah the head; BSB uses his sons and the first.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name Hebron or call Jeriah the first here; BSB supplies both.
The Hebrew has sons of Kish in the plural before Jerahmeel; BSB uses the son of Kish.
The Hebrew says according to their fathers’ house; BSB says according to their families.
